channel.title: Deep Press Analysis
channel.description: Independent analysis of corporate power, financial systems, geopolitical risk, global governance, and the infrastructure shaping economic and strategic dependencies.

item.title: State Procurement of AI Surveillance and Algorithmic Control
item.description: A systemic analysis of federal tenders in the US and EU during 2024-2026, revealing a structural shift toward the procurement of integrated AI surveillance, multimodal biometrics, and algorithmic control architectures.

item.title: ABCD Cartel and Global Food Trade: the ABCD agricultural conglomerates (ADM, Bunge, Cargill
item.description: An examination of the ABCD agricultural conglomerates (ADM, Bunge, Cargill, and Louis Dreyfus), which manage 50–60% of global trade in key crops. We analyze their transition into shadow financial institutions generating 74–76% of revenue from financial operations, the $34 billion Bunge-Viterra consolidation, the rise of state-backed competitors like COFCO and SALIC, war-related infrastructure damage in Ukraine, and the antitrust and ecological risks of blockchain data platforms and supply chains.

item.title: Global Capital Flows and Infrastructure Bottlenecks
item.description: Global capital markets are repricing three interlocking structural shifts: state-level political constraints on U.S. artificial intelligence data-center infrastructure, a de-escalation in U.S.-Iran military rhetoric that has unwound the war premium in crude oil prices, and acute fiscal, governance, and supply-chain attrition across U.S., European, and Eurasian markets.

item.title: Political Realignment and Institutional Trust
item.description: The 2028 U.S. succession takes shape as allegations surrounding political polling and corporate donations test public confidence. European unrest, changing party coalitions, artificial intelligence, and the growing cost of accessing services in Britain reveal related stresses across politics, technology, and institutions.

item.title: German-Russian Energy Dependency and Systemic Risk
item.description: A retrospective analysis of the 2007 structural warnings regarding Germany's reliance on Russian natural gas, highlighting the miscalculation of long-term political stability, the intertwining of corporate and state interests, and the inevitable fragmentation of the European energy architecture.

item.title: November 2026 Shift: US Elections, AI Energy Revolt & Geopolitics | Deep Press Analysis
item.description: An analysis of the November 2026 US midterm elections' impact on global markets, the AI infrastructure backlash, and shifting geopolitical realities in the Middle East and Ukraine.

item.title: Debt Dominance, Strait Blockades & Military Stacks
item.description: An operational synthesis of sovereign debt management shifting toward ultra-short Treasury bills and long-end buybacks, the Bank of England's rate hike to 4.00% amid a nine-month Iran conflict shock, French parliamentary rejection of the 2027 budget as 10-year OAT yields breach 5.0%, militarized transit fees and 40-fold war risk insurance increases in the Strait of Hormuz ahead of China's November 10 rare-earth export control deadline, and the convergence of defense and energy stacks around Palantir, SpaceX, and nuclear power contracts.

item.title: EU Gas Reserves Depletion: A mathematical and systemic analysis of the projected drop in European…
item.description: A mathematical and systemic analysis of the projected drop in European Union underground gas storage to below 10% by March 2027, detailing the cascading effects on physical withdrawal, summer injection, and the broader macroeconomy.

item.title: Media Divergence on AI Debt and Global Conflicts
item.description: A comparative analysis of leading Western publications reveals a systemic divergence in reporting on the US midterm elections, the burgeoning AI debt bubble, and escalating hybrid conflicts. While some outlets emphasize social crises and political lobbying, others focus on corporate vulnerabilities, regulatory arbitrage, and the redirection of insurance reserves into high-risk AI infrastructure.

item.title: Japan's Macroeconomic Bifurcation: Japan's economy undergoes a structural bifurcation as…
item.description: Japan's economy undergoes a structural bifurcation as record-breaking AI and semiconductor exports collide with a severe energy price shock, while the Bank of Japan executes its most aggressive monetary tightening in three decades.

item.title: AI Credit Freeze, Deficit Militarization & Censorship
item.description: An analytical deconstruction of the November 2, 2026 global press corpus (Financial Times, The Wall Street Journal, The Guardian, Open Magazine) examining how media focus on the U.S. midterm elections and AI technological optimism coincides with the effective closure of high-yield debt markets for "neoclouds" above 15% yields, circular vendor financing led by Nvidia's $105 billion backstop, the depletion of U.S. Patriot and THAAD air defense interceptors during the eight-month military campaign against Iran, a $6.3 billion exploit on Binance highlighting the structural boundary between censorable stablecoins and non-custodial DeFi protocols,

item.title: AI CapEx, Fiscal Extraction & Arbitrage: An analytical deconstruction of the global information…
item.description: An analytical deconstruction of the global information contour and narrative arbitrage matrix. Institutional consensus increasingly legitimizes middle-class fiscal extraction, the erosion of copyright protections for AI training, and biometric surveillance, while a major reality gap emerges between hyperscaler cash burn (-$42.4B free cash flow at Amazon) and record refining profitability ($56.3B quarterly net profit across the top five oil majors) alongside resilient decentralized finance protocols following the $6.3B Binance security breach.

item.title: Economist Narrative Audit & Political-Economic Interests
item.description: A comparative investigative audit of four issues of The Economist (July–October 2026), examining agenda shifts, internal factual discrepancies, causal reversals on oil prices and AI regulation, and documented political-economic ties.

item.title: Investment, Regulatory and Defense Signals
item.description: Seven alerts and six below-threshold findings connect insider purchases at Borr Drilling, GameStop, and Applied Digital with U.S. outbound-investment restrictions, the DeepSeek procurement ban, the November 10 BIS Affiliates Rule deadline, and expanding U.S. and European defense tenders.
